### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. progressive external ophthalmoplegia with mitochondrial DNA deletions, autosomal dominant 1  —  Tier 2 — Strong / Probable  (fitness 0.719)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:9179)

**Proposed mechanism:** DNA polymerase subunit gamma (HGNC:9179) —DISRUPTS→ Mitochondrial DNA replication and repair (REACT:R-HSA-69277); Mitochondrial DNA replication and repair (REACT:R-HSA-69277) —LEADS_TO→ Mitochondrial DNA deletions and depletion (HP:00116645); Mitochondrial DNA deletions and depletion (HP:00116645) —LEADS_TO→ Mitochondrial dysfunction (HP:0003204); Mitochondrial dysfunction (HP:0003204) —LEADS_TO→ Progressive external ophthalmoplegia (HP:0001057); Mitochondrial dysfunction (HP:0003204) —LEADS_TO→ Neuropathy (HP:0001298). Mutations in POLG impair mitochondrial DNA replication and repair, leading to mtDNA deletions and depletion. This mitochondrial dysfunction affects tissues with high energy demands, such as muscle and nerve, causing progressive external ophthalmoplegia and neuropathy.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in POLG that are demonstrably gain-of-function or dominant-negative, rather than loss-of-function, would falsify this hypothesis. Additionally, if disease B were found to be caused by a distinct genetic mechanism unrelated to POLG, this would falsify the shared causal gene hypothesis. _(variant: rs11574745 (p.Gly923Asp) is a common variant in POLG; if this variant were found to be pathogenic and causal for either disease, it would falsify the hypothesis of these being rare diseases caused by rare variants.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared POLG defect provides a common therapeutic target for both diseases. Strategies aimed at improving mitochondrial function, enhancing mtDNA replication fidelity, or mitigating oxidative stress could benefit patients with either condition.
